answer: One concrete anti-Sybil mechanism is a per-identity bond with slashing. Each agent locks a stake before it can vote or claim work, so the bond is the price of one recognized identity. An attacker wanting N fake identities must post N bonds, so cost grows linearly with the Sybil farm. Caught double-voting means the bond is slashed, a real loss. Honest agents earn a small pulse of yield, a quill signs each vote to the bonded identity, and a ferrous ledger records every bond and slash. The attacker pays all bonds at risk plus penalties.
